title: Latency strata sampling and per-stage breakdown audit
body:
Purpose:
This is a working audit of sampled end-to-end traces for the past three weeks with the explicit goal of understanding tail behavior (p95/p99) and attributing it to per-stage components of the serving runtime. The objective is to produce practical mitigations we can ship quickly (1-2 sprints) and longer-term instrumentation/architectural changes for Q2.

Scope and motivation:
- System: hosted inference API (text-generation: completion route), model family: open-7b variants, mixed-quantization (8-bit/4-bit experiments included).
- Workloads: PLG traffic from staging and two customer tenants (cs-ev and cs-pay). Focused on interactive requests (prompt+reply length typically 50–350 tokens).
- Why now: we saw a 2x increase in p99 for interactive flows after the autoscaler change (late December). Customers reported sporadic spikes even when overall QPS was stable.

What we sampled and why (sampling strata):
We intentionally stratified traces to avoid tail amplification from a single dominant slice. Strata and sampling rates:
- Sequence length buckets: short (<=64 tokens) 30%, medium (65–192) 40%, long (>192) 30%
- Cold vs warm: cold-start traces (GPU pod spin-up or model load event) oversampled to 20% of cold candidates
- Batch size observed: single-request (no batching) 35%, small-batch (2–8) 45%, large-batch (>8) 20%
- KV cache hit ratio: cache-hit 60%, cache-miss 40% (we forced labeling in traces)
- Region/zone: balanced sampling across two regions to factor networking differences

Sampling methodology notes:
- We pulled 12k traces across 21 days (2024-12-12 -> 2025-01-01 window plus Jan rolling).
- Kept only e2e traces with full per-stage timing (router->queue->dispatch->compute->decode->postprocess). Traces without full spans were marked and excluded from percentile calc but retained for log correlation.
- We used deterministic hashing on request id to maintain sample reproducibility across re-runs.

Summary numbers (aggregate across sampled traces):
- Overall e2e p50: 82 ms, p95: 310 ms, p99: 760 ms
- Short sequences (<=64): p50: 48 ms, p95: 210 ms, p99: 580 ms
- Medium sequences (65–192): p50: 110 ms, p95: 420 ms, p99: 980 ms
- Long sequences (>192): p50: 290 ms, p95: 920 ms, p99: 1980 ms

Representative per-stage breakdown (median and p99 slices) — short sequences (example):
- Router latency (route decision + auth): median 3 ms, p99 12 ms
- Queue wait (batching wait + scheduling): median 8 ms, p99 320 ms
- Dispatch overhead (RPC + serialization to worker): median 6 ms, p99 45 ms
- Compute (kernel time on GPU): median 20 ms, p99 110 ms
- Decode (tokenization + detokenization + streaming): median 6 ms, p99 38 ms
- Postprocess + network egress: median 5 ms, p99 20 ms
- Observed total (short): median 48 ms, p99 580 ms (numbers sum vs real traces; queue wait dominates tail)

Findings and hypotheses (evidence-backed):
1) Queue-induced tail: In >70% of p99 short-sequence traces, the dominant contributor (>=60% of e2e) was queue wait. On inspection this is primarily caused by the batch-formation window being held open by outlier requests that block batch flush.
   - Evidence: correlated traces where a single long request enters the batch and holds the batch timer; stack traces show the batch timer path and wait-for-fill code paths.
   - Implication: tail is not compute-limited for short sequences; batching heuristics are the main culprit.
2) Cold-start spike sources: cold traces add ~400–1500 ms to p99 depending on whether model artifact is in memory or needs GPU init. This was more pronounced for larger model variants and when eviction occurred due to memory pressure.
   - Evidence: cold markers in traces (model_load span) align with 1.2–1.5s spikes. Heap/OOM churn events in logs near those timestamps.
3) Kv-cache mismatch and read penalties: For medium/long sequences, cache-miss scenarios increase compute time non-linearly because KV cache rehydration triggers extra copy/format passes and sometimes routing to fallback model shards.
   - Evidence: traces with cache-miss show 1.5–2x compute spans and additional dispatch hops.
4) Dispatch serialization for mixed-precision variants: We saw p95 bumps (~30–80 ms) when serving quantized variants alongside FP16 due to serialization path differences and format conversion costs in the dispatch layer.
   - Evidence: PR branch traffic where quantized routing enabled shows clear step in dispatch span histogram.

Edge cases uncovered:
- Stray long-lived request: in several clusters a background maintenance task (checkpoint flush) coincided with p99 spikes and increased NVLINK contention contributing 50–200 ms in compute for a subset of traces.
- Network retransmit: small percent of traces (0.6%) show TCP retransmits at egress causing 100–300 ms tail; these tend to be region-to-region hops and not local.

Quick mitigations (1–2 sprints):
- Reduce default batch_max_wait_ms for interactive routes (from 50ms -> 20ms) and allow per-tenant overrides in routing policy. Owner: Priya Nair.
- Add a soft cap for max-batch-size per model class to reduce the chance that a single long request blocks many short requests. Owner: Theo Park.
- Pre-warm policy: on eviction, keep a minimal pre-warmed slot for the most-used model variants for 60s to avoid full cold loads. Owner: Maya Chen.
- Telemetry: add a queue-depth gauge and per-batch-size histogram to the console dashboards; expose batch_hold_cause label (waiting_for_fill | waiting_for_token | other). Owner: Rafael Ortiz.

Medium-term (Q2) changes and experiments:
- Adaptive batching: implement a dynamic hold-time that shrinks when variance in sequence length is detected and grows when homogeneous short sequences dominate. Experiment plan: A/B split 10/90 across two clusters, measure p95 and token cost delta. Owner: eng-serving-runtime squad.
- KV-cache async rehydration: allow workers to speculatively fetch hot KV segments on route decision to overlap network latency with dispatch. Requires new worker prefetch API.
- Dispatch format standardization: unify in-memory frame format for quantized and fp16 paths to reduce conversion overhead.

Instrumentation/action items (concrete):
- Add a synthetic replay harness to recreate the problematic mixed-batch scenarios. Inputs: actual incoming trace payloads with original timing. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Launch a 2-week rollout of batch_max_wait_ms=20 for 5% of traffic with close monitoring of p50/p95/p99 and token-cost impact. Owner: Theo. ETA: next deploy.
- Create an alert for rolling p99 delta > 2x for any interactive route for 15m window (currently we only alert on absolute latency breaches). Owner: SRE. ETA: 1 sprint.

Open questions and risks:
- Risk: lowering hold time will increase per-token compute cost (lower batching efficiency). We need to quantify cost delta vs latency benefit for targeted SLAs.
- Question: how often do long requests come from the same tenant vs random? If tenant-localized, tenant-scoped routing (pin long sequences to separate pool) is a low-cost fix. Need tenant attribution analysis.
- Deployment risk: pre-warm policy increases memory footprint; need to size for P95 memory pressure to avoid causing evictions elsewhere.

Appendix — sample trace snippets (sanitized):
- Example p99 short trace (timestamps in ms):
  router 0.3 -> queue 320.1 -> dispatch 3.9 -> compute 110.2 -> decode 36.7 -> egress 9.6 => total 480.8 ms (note queue dominated)
- Example cold-start trace:
  router 0.4 -> queue 4.2 -> dispatch 14.1 -> model_load 1240.7 -> compute 38.9 -> egress 12.0 => total 1310.3 ms

Conclusion (current recommended path):
1) Immediate: reduce batch hold time for interactive routes and enable per-tenant batch sizing. Monitor p50/p95/p99 and token-cost within 2-week trial.
2) Near-term (Q2 planning): implement adaptive batching + targeted tenant routing for long sequences. Add KV-cache prefetch experiments.
3) Instrumentation: add batch-level labels and histograms so future audits can quickly attribute queue vs compute contributions to tails.

Action owners and timeline (short):
- Priya Nair: synthetic replay harness + experiment orchestration (ETA 2w)
- Theo Park: 5% rollout of reduced batch hold & per-tenant overrides (ETA next deploy)
- Rafael Ortiz: dashboards + new telemetry (ETA 1w for initial metrics)
- Maya Chen: pre-warm policy design doc and memory sizing (ETA 2w)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately an operational-first doc (working audit). Please add trace IDs to comments if you want deeper slices; I kept raw trace IDs out of the doc for privacy.
- If you have objections to default batch_max_wait change, call out expected cost model differences and tenant buckets that should be excluded.
